title: Stitching Methods for Drone Panos: Rectilinear and 360 Workflows with PTGui, Panavolo, and Lightroom

date.basis: embedded_creation_time in metadata; filename indicates production period around 2026

summary: The video surveys how to create panoramic drone images, emphasizing how lens choice and stitching method affect distortion and output. It contrasts rectilinear stitching with spherical/panometric options, explains when to use a wide-angle panel versus a free panel, and compares tools (Lightroom, Photoshop, PTGui Pro, and Panavolo). The instructor demonstrates exposure matching, perspective warping, and cropping decisions, with a deep dive into 360-degree panoramas, mirroring techniques for center alignment, and batch workflows (Lightroom and image processor) to prepare inputs for Panovolo. Practical tips include shooting on auto exposure for large tonal ranges, avoiding extreme edge distortion, and choosing projections (rectilinear, stereographic, cylindrical) to shape the final composition.
